capability_and_deadline_matching.verdict: needs other robots' positions and schedules; positions are excluded from the relay by design (invariant 10)

coordinator_only.verdict: there is no coordinator addressable in the subscriber space; this is an architecture change, not a routing rule

current_coalition.verdict: recipients are the robots already told about the target, so a newly discovered one has an empty set: every first report is addressed to nobody, and under the isolated path an unreceived task can never enter any robot's action list (source map question 9)

global_broadcast.verdict: the status quo; a constant fan-out adds no choice

radio_neighbourhood.verdict: no per-robot position or range view exists in the transcript or the observation; only an artificial radius could supply one

R3_observable_before_the_action.reason: SendObservation exposes one scalar `subscribers` for the whole step (comm_policy.py:112), not a per-candidate recipient set, and SendItem carries only `members_changed: bool` -- no member list. The contract has no place to put 'whom would this go to'.

condition_1_first_report_price_differenc.note: broadcast reaches 16/16 only through a median 6-byte difference driven by serialized field lengths, not by recipients, so it satisfies the letter of condition 1 and violates condition 5

condition_4_not_only_refresh_choices.note: the heterogeneity coalition routing buys is entirely on the refresh side; the first-report side collapses to an empty recipient set

condition_5_difference_from_real_semanti.reason: any global change of fan-out is provably equivalent to rescaling the budget (see R1's claim 2), so it is the scaling route the protocol forbids
